implementation.line_layout_cache: gpui/text_cache.go (new, 259 lines): the port of the reference LineLayoutCache (crates/gpui/src/text_system/line_layout.rs:925-1127 at 254b5dbd…). Two frame maps (previous/current) of shapedLineKey -> *WrappedLine; layoutWrappedLine consults current, then previous (a hit moves into the current frame), and only a full miss shapes through the TextSystem; finishFrame swaps the frames and disposes the old previous frame's leftovers — the entries the finishing frame did not request — which is where the Rust Arc's last reference would die. Key = the reference CacheKey (text, font size, runs, wrap width, line clamp) in a Go-comparable shape: the run list length-prefix-encoded into one canonical string (deep-equal run lists produce equal keys whatever their slice provenance); floats by IEEE-754 bits. sync_font_generation ported with a recorded deviation: the generation is read off the fresh layout (the only place the native ABI exposes it) instead of a standalone platform query, so a stale generation is discovered one shape late — same clear, same trigger. Locking: one Mutex (the reference's Mutex+RwLock pair collapsed; the port has no concurrent layout readers). Not ported: reuse_layouts/truncate_layouts and the used-lines bookkeeping — they exist for the reference's deferred-draw paint-range reuse (window.rs:3719-3820), which the port does not have (its deferred draws re-request layouts), recorded in the file header.
implementation.wiring: gpui/div.go: realWindowTextSystem gains the lines shapedLineCache (the reference WindowTextSystem's per-window line_layout_cache) and shape resolves through layoutWrappedLine (the reference shape_text path); the windowTextSystem seam interface gains finishFrame (the reference WindowTextSystem::finish_frame), a no-op on the deterministic test system (gpui/testwindow.go). gpui/inline_real.go: shapeRuns (the inline paragraph's per-segment shaping) resolves through the same cache, so both real shaped paths — the text element's measure seam and the inline path — reuse lines across frames. gpui/render.go: completeFrame calls ds.text.finishFrame() at the window draw's tail (window.rs:3230 self.text_system().finish_frame()); an abandoned build does not finish the frame, like the reference — its entries stay for the next completed frame's rotation, nothing leaks either way. gpui/element.go: dropDrawState disposes the cache's lines with the window's element runtime (next to the atlas slot) — the reference window's Arc-held lines die with its WindowTextSystem. The dead inlineShapedLines frame map (registered in inline_real.go, never actually disposed anywhere) is removed: the cache now owns every real line's lifetime.
implementation.observable: gpui/text.go: TextSystem.LiveShapingHandles() — the Go-side mirror of the native service's live-handle count (every handle flows through ShapeText/Dispose, so the atomic counter tracks it exactly; the native ABI exposes only its bound MaxShapingHandles). Additive public API, no behavior change.
implementation.editor_disposal: gpui/editor.go: currentDocument disposes the superseded document's handle at the version-gated refresh (the reference drops the old Arc; the port owns the handle explicitly) — the input field's model otherwise accumulated one live handle per text change (typing 256+ changes exhausted the bound the same way).

limitations: The cache is per-window (the reference's per-WindowTextSystem scope), not process-global: the public TextSystem.ShapeText keeps its uncached, caller-disposes semantics (the mordbard hand-built-scene workaround's contract is unchanged). The ticket's 'cross-frame shaped-line cache in TextSystem' is realized at the reference's own layer — the window text system seam that the element pipeline shapes through.

Disposal happens at the frame rotation and window teardown, not under Go GC: a *WrappedLine handed out by the cache must not be disposed by its consumer (the shapedText seam's contract, the reference handing out Arc clones). The port's scene paint rasterizes glyphs at paint time and retains no line, so eviction at finish_frame is safe.

An abandoned frame build leaves its entries for the next completed frame's rotation (the reference's panic behavior — no clear on unwind); the entries are bounded by the failed frame's distinct keys and release at the next rotation or window close.
reuse_layouts/truncate_layouts (the deferred-draw paint-range reuse) and the used-lines bookkeeping are not ported — the port's deferred draws re-request layouts; recorded in text_cache.go's header.

The font-generation invalidation is discovered one shape late (the native ABI exposes the generation per layout, not as a query); with no font-registration path yet (ticket 03), the trigger is currently unreachable — the port is ready for it.

The Editor's final document line (the version-gated refresh's last shape) is disposed only on the next version change, not at Editor teardown — the reference's Arc dies with the Editor; the port's Editor has no Dispose lifecycle in this slice (one bounded handle per live editor, not per text change).
LiveShapingHandles is a Go-side mirror, exact because every native handle is issued and disposed through the Go adapter; it is not a native query (the ABI has none).
